# wake v0.3.2

v0.3.2 moves quota recovery out of blind 15-minute model retries and into a
lightweight local watcher.

## Highlights

- Reads Codex quota locally through `codex app-server`.
- Uses `ordinaryUsageAllowed` as the authoritative recovery signal.
- Registers the exact current thread from `CODEX_THREAD_ID`.
- Tracks `monitoring -> quota_waiting -> monitoring`.
- Resumes only exact registered threads that actually observed quota blocking.
- Never uses `--last` or guesses a thread id.
- WAITING_USER threads remain paused even when quota recovers.
- Adds Windows `.cmd` helpers to avoid common PowerShell execution-policy friction.
- Keeps Scheduled Tasks as a conservative fallback.

## Tested

Quota reads were verified with Codex CLI 0.156.1 on Windows, including an
exhausted 5-hour window returning `ordinaryUsageAllowed: false` and a future
`resetsAt`.

## Known limitation

The watcher currently resumes quota-blocked work using detached
`codex exec resume <thread-id>`. Exact identity is preserved, but Codex Desktop
may not always render that continuation exactly like a native Desktop turn.

WAKE does not bypass quotas, rate limits, credits, or safety controls.
